Argument for “Contrived Primitiveness” (Debater_A’s Position)

I reaffirm that Earth’s involvement with Skkiru’s planet is an anthropological “field trip,” not resource extraction. The Snaddrath have gone to extreme lengths—at grave cost—to appear primitive and lure repeated Terran expeditions for “pleasure and profit in intensive analysis” (<invalid_quote>“pleasure and profit…intensive analysis”</invalid_quote>). I will show all anomalies vanish under the cultural‐evaluation theory but multiply under the extraction theory.

1. Resource Hostility, Not Exploitation  
  • “Our old culture was too much like the Terrans’ own to be of interest” (<quote>p.


</quote>). If Earth truly sought raw materials, similarity would not deter them; it would ease extraction.  
  • Prohibitions on “air-cars and self‐levitation…insufficiently primitive” (<quote>p.


</quote>) sabotage transport and supply lines—counterproductive if minerals or labor were goals.  
  • “Food and fiber had to be brought from the other planets at fabulous expense” (<quote>p.


</quote>). A resource‐hungry power would develop local agriculture and industry, not enforce “wetter season” exposure to starve the population.  
  • Skkiru’s secret use of air‐car pontoons (<quote>p.


</quote>) and his hidden transportation gear prove the surface regime is unsustainable—only a charade to sustain the “primitive” tableau for Terrans.

2. Artificial Caste and Token Gifts  
  • Metal‐workers, the only repository of metallurgy, are pariahs segregated by “chain of their own devising” (<quote>p.


</quote>) while Bbulas alone dons spun‐metal underskirts and contact‐lenses (<invalid_quote>pp. 22–23</invalid_quote>). Why exile essential technicians if you intend mining? Because their absence enhances “otherness.”  
  • Chocolate gift: “Only in the most expensive…shops…Skkiru ate the candy then and there” (<quote>p.


</quote>). Currency and luxury are superfluous to a “genuine primitive” but irresistible to Terrans. Skkiru suspects Bbulas wants to “contribute it later to the Treasury,” i.e., the Planetary Budget for future missions.  
  • Bbulas hoards “antique blueprints” of huts from rare dealers (<quote>p.


</quote>). A real primitive society would generate its own plans; a curated exhibit uses expensive pre‐existing models to save time and control findings.

3. Overt “Professions” of Objectivity  
  • “We promise to make our intensive analysis…painless” and “we wish only to study your society, not to tamper” (<quote>p.


</quote>) are classic colonial euphemisms. Genuine exploitation would resort to direct trade, treaties, or force, not lengthy “rapport” and “rain dances.”  
  • Terrans complain of cannibal Glotch mission “we let the missionaries get first crack…soften them up” (<quote>p.


</quote>). This is familiar anthropological method: deploy local puppet culture to gather data, then leave—hence repeated visits.

4. Rituals Contrary to Genuine Need  
  • “Rain dance…to stop rain” (<quote>p.


</quote>) in a world drowning in mud. If resource transport relied on dry land, they would welcome rain, not suppress it. This dance is a performance intended for observers, not a genuine agricultural need, as Snaddrath “borrowed” ritual forms from “fictapes” (<quote>p.


</quote>).  
  • “Language of the stomach…universal” (<quote>p.


</quote>) and “rain dance” are performative spectacles, not functional rites.

5. Inadequate Population Control  
  • “No need for birth‐control measures” yet “population…dwindling” (<quote>p.


</quote>) despite “vulgar fecund” Terrans. A resource‐driven agent would encourage population to supply labor and markets. The enforced stagflation of Snaddra preserves the exotic sample size.

Objections to Debater_B’s Resource Theory  
A. “Profit” Does Not Necessarily Mean Resources  
  • “Profit” can mean scientific prestige and future grant funding. Phrases like “carry our affection back” (<quote>p.


</quote>) emphasize cultural propaganda, not trade proposals.  
  • “Intensive analysis” is clearly an anthropological term; genuine survey missions rarely claim “no tampering” if resource rights are the goal.

B. Lack of Export Mechanisms  
  • No mention of off‐world shipping of local products or minerals. All advanced machinery remains underground or confiscated from outcasts. Even air‐cars are withheld.  
  • No treaties or agreements for import–export; Terrans are merely “guests” invited to ceremonies.

C. Tabus and Secrecy  
  • “Don’t forget your shoes…except the beggar” (<quote>p.


</quote>) and “libel laws…very severe” to hide underground cities. True colonization would secure full access to all regions.  
  • The “chain of metal-workers” discourages any local metallurgy visible on surface. A resource‐hungry expedition would license skilled miners, not ostracize them.

D. Contradiction of “Primitive” Praise  
  • Raoul praises mud: “such texture…aroma” (<quote>p.


</quote>), but then complains of rains. Their inconsistent preferences betray an agenda to prolong discomfort for observation.  
  • Raoul’s fear of “man-eaters” (<quote>p.


</quote>) and their swift retreat from Glotch show they avoid genuine risk: they never claim Snaddra is dangerous or hostile enough to expel them, guaranteeing longer stays.

Conclusion  
Only the contrived‐primitiveness explanation accounts for:  
• The enforced inefficiencies and hidden technology;  
• The orchestrated spectacles (rain dances, beggar‐priest romance);  
• The repeated, “painless” analyses with no tangible extraction;  
• The secrecy about true society;  
• Skkiru’s only hope being further Terran visits to restore his role.  
Debater_B’s resource theory cannot explain the anti‐technological tabus, absence of export, nor the crippling cost Snaddra bears to maintain the ruse. Therefore, Earth’s entanglement is anthropological evaluation of a forced primitive exhibit, not straightforward resource exploitation.
